name: FormFactor, Inc.

evidence.excerpt: FormFactor, Inc. (Exact name of registrant as specified in its charter) ... Securities registered pursuant to Section 12(b) of the Act: Title of each class Trading Symbol(s) Name of each exchange on which registered Common stock, $0.001 par value FORM Nasdaq Global Select Market

notes: COMPARATOR ENTITY. FormFactor is registered as a foreign incumbent, not as part of the Chinese equipment supply base: its revenue must never be totalled into a domestic figure, and entity_class foreign_incumbent is what the analysis layer filters on to prevent that. It is registered here because it is the global incumbent against which the atlas's test_probe_card comparison is measured: the atlas holds MaxOne (Qiangyi, entity_id qiangyi_semiconductor) at test_probe_card as its only Chinese entity in that step, and FormFactor's own FY2025 10-K Competition section names 'Max One' among its probe-card competitors (physical p8 of that filing), alongside Micronics Japan Co., Ltd. ('MJC' in this atlas's own priority queue for this step). FormFactor is also the HBM-exposed half of the test-side comparator set: probe cards are a consumable interface consumed per wafer tested, and FormFactor's own FY2025 10-K MD&A attributes the growth in its DRAM probe-card market specifically to 'increased demand for HBM designs utilized in generative artificial intelligence applications' in three consecutive fiscal years (FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025) -- see the application_links file for the exact passages. Advantest is already registered as this atlas's memory-tester comparator (test_memory_ate), so FormFactor at test_probe_card completes the test side of the HBM tool chain. Incorporated in Delaware, headquartered in Livermore, California; NASDAQ Global Select Market ticker FORM; SEC CIK 0001039399. Reports in US dollars, never converted. FormFactor operates on a 52/53-week fiscal year ending the last Saturday of December (its own words, FY2025 10-K physical p5): FY2025 ran 29 Dec 2024-27 Dec 2025 (52 weeks), FY2024 ran 31 Dec 2023-28 Dec 2024 (52 weeks), FY2023 ran 1 Jan 2023-30 Dec 2023 (52 weeks), FY2022 ran 26 Dec 2021-31 Dec 2022 (53 weeks, a 14-week fourth quarter) and FY2021 ran 27 Dec 2020-25 Dec 2021 (52 weeks); none of these is the calendar year, and FY2022 in particular is not comparable week-for-week to the 52-week years either side of it. FormFactor operates two reportable segments, Probe Cards (probe cards and analytical probes) and Systems (probe stations, thermal systems and cryogenic systems, plus metrology systems until the Q4 FY2023 sale of the FRT business); within Probe Cards it discloses a further 'Revenues by Market' split into Foundry & Logic, DRAM and Flash, which is the finest product granularity it gives and is filed as such -- never allocated further. NO ALIAS IN ANY LANGUAGE OTHER THAN ENGLISH was located in any of the three filings held for this packet; none is supplied. HBM DISCLOSURE: FormFactor names HBM repeatedly in narrative (Item 1 Business product description, Competition section, and MD&A revenue-driver commentary in every fiscal year held) but discloses no HBM-specific revenue figure, unit count or percentage-of-DRAM split anywhere in the three 10-Ks reviewed -- a clean null, consistent with four of the six first-wave comparators publishing nothing finer than the atlas's Chinese side. FormFactor also states explicitly that it does not carry a backlog sufficient to meet quarterly revenue targets ('we generally do not have a sufficient backlog of unfilled orders...'), so no order_backlog observation is registered here: this is a disclosed absence, not a gap in extraction. No named commercial platform/model (e.g. no product-line trade name analogous to ASMPT's 'TC Next' or Besi's named models) appears anywhere in the three 10-Ks; FormFactor's own product disclosure stays at the category level (Probe Cards, Analytical Probes, Probe Stations, Thermal Subsystems, Cryogenic Systems), so no platform record is registered for this packet.
